That maps exactly to Image Browser — a local-first Tauri 2 + Rust desktop application I built and shipped, with a 28-file Rust backend, dual-connection SQLite WAL (writer Mutex plus a read-only secondary via OnceLock), three ONNX-Runtime image encoders fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion, single-flight indexing with an AtomicBool RAII guard, and zero post-launch network calls except the first-launch model fetch.

Two other responsibilities anchor the same fit. "Scalability: Enhancing software development lifecycle, tools, and processes" is the principle behind Cernio (my 14k-LOC Rust + Ratatui + SQLite job-discovery engine): 6 ATS provider fetchers behind a tokio::Semaphore-capped HTTP client, a lib+bin split that unblocked tests/, 346 inline + integration tests, and preferences.toml as a typed runtime config surface guarded by 21 build-time integrity tests. "Writing clear, concise, and testable code" is the discipline of Nyquestro (my deterministic limit-order matching engine): single-threaded by design, zero unsafe, snapshot-and-compare quote emission, four-phase submit_limit, and an architectural import graph that mechanically prevents the December 2025 coupling regression from re-emerging.
why_company:
Proton is the rare company where the product architecture and my engineering instincts agree on first principles. The company builds Proton Mail, Proton VPN, Proton Calendar, Proton Drive, and Proton Pass — end-to-end encryption across all products — and is non-VC profitable on user subscriptions, founded by CERN scientists, supporting 100M+ accounts. The Inbox Desktop team's mission is specifically to rebuild the Mail Desktop App on a cross-platform Rust stack while preserving the end-to-end encryption guarantees and the user-experience bar.

Image Browser is the project where I made the same architectural commitment without anyone asking me to: it is local-first by construction, has zero post-launch network calls outside the first-launch HuggingFace model download (~2.5 GB across 7 files), puts every user-data write through a single writer Mutex<Connection> with a read-only secondary connection for SELECT, and emits no telemetry by default. Proton's company-wide "privacy is the default" stance is the production-grade version of the discipline I have been writing for myself, and the Mail Desktop App is the canonical project on which to apply it. The Inbox team's flat, science-rooted, psychologically-safe framing also matches the engineering culture I have been practising across my OSS work — claim-then-implement on issue threads, draft PRs as direction-forcing artefacts, maintainer-voice notes captured per-repo before opening anything.
technical_project:
Image Browser is my closest technical analogue to the Inbox Desktop App rebuild. The problem: local image libraries grow to tens of thousands of files; existing tooling (Finder, Photos) cannot do semantic search, and every cloud-based alternative either uploads the library or requires an account. I wanted a Pinterest-style masonry browser and a search bar that accepted natural language ("snowy mountain at sunset") or a sample image and returned visually-similar matches — entirely offline, on a single laptop.

The approach: Tauri 2 (Rust backend, React 19 frontend), three ONNX-Runtime image encoders (CLIP ViT-B/32, DINOv2-Base, SigLIP-2 Base 256) running in parallel with their rank lists fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Cormack 2009, k=60), persisted in SQLite WAL via bytemuck::cast_slice for the embedding column. Single-flight indexing with an AtomicBool + RAII RunningGuard(Drop) so rapid filesystem events coalesce; a notify watcher with 5-second debounce; multi-section settings drawer driven by useUserPreferences (localStorage).

Specific techniques worth naming. The first cut had a single Mutex<Connection> for the whole DB; under sustained ingest the foreground ipc.get_images call was blocked behind writer batches and triggered a 22-second freeze (perf-1777212369). The fix was a dual-connection pattern: writer Mutex<Connection> for mutations plus a read-only secondary opened via OnceLock<Mutex<Connection>> for SELECTs — read traffic no longer blocks behind writes, which closed the freeze. CoreML is disabled for all encoders on macOS because it produces runtime errors for transformer ops; on M2, intra_threads(4) + inter_threads(1) serialises op execution across the four P-cores instead of over-subscribing, with a dynamic intra = N / enabled_encoders adjustment when multiple encoders run in the same session. A code-health audit later removed three unsafe sites in favour of bytemuck::cast_slice for the embedding columns.

The measurable outcome: image-search latency lands under 200ms across libraries of ~10,000 images on an M2 MacBook Air, with zero post-launch network traffic and the 22-second foreground freeze eliminated by the dual-connection SQLite split. The same single-flight + RAII-guard discipline now anchors the indexing pipelines in two of my later projects.
cover_letter:
Dear Proton Inbox Desktop team,

I'm applying for the Rust Software Engineer role on Proton Inbox Desktop. The description's framing — "rebuilding our client applications on a new, innovative technology stack centered around cross-platform Rust code," explicit acceptance of "complex Rust pet projects" alongside professional experience, and ownership across research, work breakdown, scalability, and mentoring — is precisely the work I have been deliberately building toward across 8 active Rust projects and 9 vetted upstream OSS engagements (most recently burn PR #4894, +1864 LOC, merged 2026-05-11).

My closest technical match is Image Browser: a local-first Tauri 2 + Rust desktop image library where I shipped a 28-file Rust backend, dual-connection SQLite WAL (a fix that eliminated a 22-second ipc.get_images foreground freeze by separating writer and reader connections), three ONNX-Runtime encoders fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion, a single-flight indexing pipeline with an AtomicBool + RAII guard, and zero post-launch network calls outside a first-launch HuggingFace model download. Nyquestro (my deterministic limit-order matching engine, zero unsafe, single-threaded MVP), Cernio (14k-LOC Rust + Ratatui + SQLite job-discovery engine with 346 tests and a lib+bin split for testability), and Tessarix (Tauri 2 with tauri::ipc::Channel<StreamEvent> for per-token SSE streaming) extend the same muscle to adjacent shapes.

What pulls me to Proton specifically is the alignment between architecture and principle. Image Browser is local-first because I made that choice without anyone asking me to; Proton makes it the company's first commitment, on top of CERN-scientist engineering rigour, non-VC profitability, and 100M+ user accounts. The Inbox Desktop team's mission — rebuild the Mail Desktop App on cross-platform Rust while preserving end-to-end encryption guarantees — is the production version of the discipline I have been practising on my own time, on a system 100 million users depend on.

Visa note: I hold a UK Graduate Visa valid through 7 August 2027 (unrestricted UK right-to-work during that window); Skilled Worker sponsorship would be required from August 2027 onwards. Happy to discuss the London-vs-Geneva split during a conversation. Thank you for the role and for the work Proton ships.

Ata Caner Cetinkaya
